text:
priya: quick follow-up to the hotpatch RFC — proposing a minimal sidecar-based path for shipping signed CUDA / driver micro-patches to air-gapped onprem clusters. sketch below, want tradeoff feedback.

dan: show me the sketch pls. worried about kernel-module reboots on customer infra.

priya: yeah, that's the sticky bit. idea is: bundle driver userland shim + verified kernel module delta signed by our signing key. operator-sidecar orchestrates an atomic swap sequence:
```
1) upload signed delta to operator (airgapped via USB/registry import)
2) sidecar verifies signature + hash via onboard verifier
3) sidecar places delta in staged path (immutable filename)
4) gracefully drain serving pods using ephemeral CPU-fallback
5) orchestrate kernel module replace with fallback policy and health probes
6) on success, promote staged -> active and prune old modules
```

maya: can we avoid kernel module touches entirely by using a userland fallback shim that can intercept GPU calls?

priya: partial — userland shim works for some runtimes (CUDA user APIs), but not for kernel-level driver fixes (nv-hostengine, PCI hotplug handling). for perf-critical fixes you need kernel bits.

sam: what about rollback safety? if a module fails to load we need guaranteed safe fallback so customer workloads don't OOM/abort.

priya: rollback plan: keep previous signed artifact available locally (don't gc until 24h), and operator will attempt auto-rollback on health-check failure. also policy flag to force manual rollback only for clusters with strict audit.

ciara: storage constraints: many airgapped customers have tiny /var and long retention policies. shipping multiple driver copies is heavy.

priya: proposal: delta-only payloads (binary diffs) + content-addressed chunks, small local cache size (configurable). plus optional NVRAM staging path if admin provides it. chunking helps keep payloads < 50MB typical.

dan: signing/attestation: who verifies what? we need to avoid complex root-of-trust setups for customers.

priya: keep it simple: operator ships our public verification key, pinned at install. operator verifier supports key rotation via offline-escrow workflow (signed rotation manifest). we log verification chain to local audit log and expose it in Console later.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: new artifact uploaded to operator: artifact-id=art-2026-06-04-03, size=38MB, signature=sha256:abcd... :white_check_mark:

maya: question about testing: can we run a dry-run that loads module into isolated namespace and runs smoke tests without affecting main workloads?

priya: yes — sidecar can mount a test-ns via CRI sandbox, load module there, run smoke script (we'll supply a small test harness), then proceed to drain/prod. helps avoid noisy production failures.

sam: compliance and audit: need to capture ACL changes and operator actions in an immutable audit artifact customers can ship to SOC teams.

priya: agreed — operator will emit a signed audit blob (JSON) with action, artifact ids, verifier result, and outcome. admin can export via the console or CLI.

ciara: performance impact during swap — expected 10-30s to drain and swap for small clusters, more for larger. we should document SLO impact and have automatic fallback to CPU-only nodes if defined.

priya: tradeoffs summary I want feedback on:
- Pros: smaller deltas, ability to ship urgent fixes without full image updates, audit trail, configurable safety gates.
- Cons: kernel touches still risky, operator privileges escalate (requires CAP_SYS_MODULE or helper), storage complexity for retention, more moving pieces in airgapped support.

dan: my main blocker is operator privilege. can we do helper VM that performs module install with tighter isolation instead of granting CAP_SYS_MODULE to operator?

priya: yes — alternative path: small privileged installer binary that runs as a short-lived job (owned by admin) instead of long-lived privileged operator. requires out-of-band scheduling but reduces attack surface.

maya: +1 for the short-lived privileged job option. also add an opt-in telemetry contract for success/failure events (customer-controlled).

priya: thanks — i'll update the RFC with two modes: "sidecar-orchestrated" (operator does orchestration, less admin work) and "ephemeral-installer" (admin-triggered, lower privilege). will add a runbook for rollback, signature rotation, and retention defaults.

sam: please include a clear matrix of which fixes can be userland-only vs kernel-required. that'll help sales and support.

priya: will do. tagging @ciara @dan @maya for final comments before I fold into RFC v2. :memo:

ciara: left a couple inline comments in the doc.

priya: great — thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
